summary: An 1858 iron skeleton tower on the outer Florida Reef off Marathon, the tallest of the six Florida Reef Lights; deactivated in 2015 and sold at auction in 2022.

access.note: Privately owned since a 2022 federal auction; tower closed and declared unsafe to climb by the Coast Guard. Viewed from a distance.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NRHP nomination says automated in 1960; LighthouseFriends says personnel were pulled off 23 October 1962; USLHS roster shows Coast Guard personnel through 1962. Story states the disagreement.
The light was deactivated in 2015 when the Coast Guard moved the aid to a new nearby tower; the record's 'still lit' disagreement refers to the new tower or older lists.
NRHP says about 154 feet; Bulletin 1937 says 160 feet; record has 43.3 m (142 ft), which is the focal plane. Story reports the NRHP and Bulletin figures.

notes_for_editor: No Chronicling America hits for Sombrero Key + Rieke 1893-94; the 1873 and 1893 incidents rest on LighthouseFriends (which quotes the station journal and lists the Philadelphia Record of 6 Nov 1893) and are footnoted to it as second-hand. LighthouseFriends writes 'In 2105' for the deactivation (typo for 2015). It also says the sale failed for 'Sand Key' where Sombrero Key is meant; the story uses Keys Weekly and the NHLPA report. Fabal's keeper dates differ between the 1924 Bulletin obituary (keeper from 1903) and the USLHS roster (head 1913-1919, Watkins 1904-1913). Hurricane date of 1926 item is inferred from the 1926 Bulletin volume and LighthouseFriends (Oct 1926); the Bulletin item itself gives 17-20 Oct without the year. Bulletin page numbers are PDF pages from corpus.py grep; the 1893 Light-House Board OCR is poor (scan pages 22 and 152), quotes copied with OCR errors. Bulletin 1929 letter quoted in clean form from LighthouseFriends' transcription. LHB 1893 gives 29 and 30 April for the sectors change. NRHP listing year not stated in story (record says 2012). NRHP OCR is imperfect; quotes chosen from clean passages. LF says Hurricane Donna and the 1959 death; not independently verified in a primary record.
